title: FOOTBALL | Head Coach Jeff Lebby Press Conference - 11/21/26
text: Yeah, I did. I wanted to start with just saying thanks to fans, donors, everybody that has supported us as we've gone through this stretch. There's been a ton of adversity. And I'm not not going to sit here and make excuses. At the end of the day, man, it is my job to make sure our football team is constantly ready to go play and ready to go win. But so thankful for again our fan base, our donors who have Man, they have. They They've been all in. Appreciate our seniors for their last time in Davis Wade and being able to go win today. They've meant a ton to me and our program. A couple of these guys as I walked in the door three years ago, man, they've stayed the course and been incredibly consistent. So humbling for me to be able to go out there with them today and and go one and 0. A ton of people inside our community, inside our university that make this thing go. Seniors in the band, cheer squad, spirit squad, everybody that helps us and get the chance to do what we do. And so thankful for them as Again, this was their last opportunity in Davis Wade as well. So big one next Friday. And we got a ton to play for. And so great urgency from our guys as we we get ready to roll for that one on Friday. So with that, I'll open it up. >> I I know you got a a good result, but maybe not the start you wanted. I mean, you come out and took some shots early. What did you kind of do to settle Billy down? Cuz it seems like he threw some much better balls as the game went along. >> Yeah, he did. He He settled down and we were able to hit on some things. Really frustrating that we started the game obviously the way that we did. Wanted to be really aggressive early to be able to try to help us in the run game with some things that we had planned. We don't hit on them. We get the 5-yd penalty on punt. Then we don't convert on the fourth and one with at at tied end, which was again inexcusable and really frustrating because then we put on the field right there at midfield. Um and then again for us, [clears throat] as we looked up, we we did. We created some chunks and the chunk plays helped us in a huge way. Did not like the fact that we settled for the two field goals there uh early on. Really a struggle once we got down in the red zone and not being able to again man be really good on first and second down to to give us a chance to score touchdowns. The penalties uh called two of them back we got to play cleaner with alignment down field and the holding. But I thought Billy tried to come back after not starting the way we wanted to and and did some good things. Didn't like the turnover down there in the red area obviously. >> And with Billy just what do you think getting this first career win means for him personally with everything that's gone on in the quarterback room this season and also just his journey here to Mississippi State? >> No, it means a ton to him. I'm incredibly appreciative of of Bill and who he's been. The kid absolutely loves our university, loves this football team, loves his teammates, wants to play better and better, wants to give us an opportunity to go win. And so for him to get that done today, you know, proud of him. >> No matter how it happened, you end a six game losing streak and you guys have just been kind of treading water trying to get back to that. What was it like just getting back in the locker room with your guys and being able to celebrate for the first time in a couple of months? >> Yeah, I told him like I'm not I 'm not going to take the win for granted. I will never do that. At the same time, we got a big one Friday. And our urgency and how we're getting ready to go do what we need to do next Friday matters in a great way. Again, that and that's why I started with the opening statement of the seniors, how appreciative I am of them, them being able to go out the right way today. Really really good. We didn't play good enough today. And for us, it's about playing as good as we can possibly play next Friday morning in Oxford to go win and and get that trophy back home. >> What do you feel like led to the wide receivers having as good of a day as they ended up having? >> Yeah, we did. We had good matchups out there on the perimeter. We missed on some things too. Obviously had some explosives called back because of the penalties. But we did. We had really good matchups. We've had good matchups. That that's not going to change. We've got to be able to do what we need to do up front and be able to stand in the pocket and be able to go deliver the football when we've got guys open. And so we were able to do that a little bit more today. We're going to need it next Friday. >> We've often talked about the speed of Xavier gotten and he really showed it on that touchdown run. Just what have you seen from him lately to give him that opportunity? >> Yeah, we we did. We wanted to get X in the game to give him a couple of opportunities. He's continued to do some really good things for us. Obviously he's played really well for us on teams. He's had limited reps offensively. But what you love is he gets that opportunity and he is. As soon as he got in the open field, you know, all of us knew that he was going to be able to go score. So really good to create that chunk play in the run game as we were coming out right there. >> I know he left the game hurt after the punt return fumble, but Anthony Evans, the way he celebrated that touchdown seemed like he was kind of breaking free from the frustration that he's had. What did you see from him and how how good was it to see him break open again? >> Yeah, he did some really good things for us today. He he is. He's he's going to be fine. Really frustrated with his decision in that moment after we get a three and out, we get off the field. That has not been him in two years to make that decision back there at that moment is very out of character. So that that was frustrating. He did. He made some some really good plays that we needed him to make to be able to create some cushion. >> F two, let's start with Isaiah Dent starting at left tackle. Obviously you made a change this week and that is that a byproduct of that change and and how do you feel like he played? >> Yeah, Isaiah did some good things. Obviously the hold was on him, you know, on the touchdown getting called back late. He could have finished in a little better body position. Really proud of him uh for being able to go play uh today and get the start and and we'll continue to evaluate that as we move it forward. >> You mentioned how you know big the game is next week. I mean did that factor into some decisions to kind of hold some guys out, get them 100% you know because I know Fluff didn't play this week and there were a couple other guys. I know you want to win the game but you got to think about the full season. >> No I I was I was very dialed in on today and we needed our guys that were healthy to go play really well. Fluff wasn't quite ready to play. Um you know even this morning in the hotel he's chomping at the bit to go play. It wasn't the right thing to do uh trying to get him back to as close to 100% as we can for Friday. >> I feel like we haven't been talking much about Dray Bledsoe but he's seems to be making a lot of money this year what he's doing on the defensive line. What's been the thing for him that has really flipped this year to allow him to be so dominant inside? >> He has continued to develop and that guy has played really really well and Robbie you're right we have not talked about him a ton but he has played his butt off for us inside and uh he's putting himself in a position uh man to continue to play this game for a long time. So really proud of Dray. We knew we were getting a really really athletic interior player. Uh man that guy's played his butt off and and and proud of him. Proud of him cuz he's about to get his degree here in about 3 weeks which is awesome. >> Coach it felt like Tennessee Tech was able to move the ball but you are you guys were able to stop them in some some key moments. Um compared to last week what did you like from your defense today? What did you see out of them? >> I I thought once they got in the red zone we did we found a way to get off the field. Really frustrating with some of the pass defense. Not not good enough. They did they made some plays on us one on one which was frustrating when we were in zone coverage there was a little too much air so some frustrating moments. Again our guys have responded the right way and they've continued just to play the next play. We've played great red zone defense this year, much improved. And we're going to need that again on on Friday. But obviously the best red zone defense is not letting them get down there, so plenty to clean up. >> What do the next 24 hours look like for you getting ready for for next Friday? >> Yeah, as soon as I walk out of the stadium I'll be on to the next one. So be be watching these guys all day every day until we get ready to roll. So our week speeds up obviously with it being a short week. But we've had that plan the entire time, so there's been work go into these guys. Whether it was on the open date or maybe me stealing some some time at at some other points to be able to to get a head start. >> Is there any chance that Swann could play in the Egg Bowl or is that still kind of being decided? >> It'll still kind of being decided. Obviously you guys saw him today in his in the boot, you know, so he is he is better today than he was obviously on Monday. He wasn't close to being ready to play today. The hope is that he will be ready to roll, but it it's going to be day to day, especially with it being as short of a week as it is. >> Talk about what the process is like of sticking to your identity of who you are as a coach and balancing that with just doing what it takes to win even if it might go against that identity. >> Yeah, I mean for us the job of a coach is to put their football team in position to go win and and have great success. So for me I'm going to continue to be exactly who I'm supposed to be. That's the only way I'm I'm ever going to do it. I got great confidence in that. I got great conviction in that. And for us as we continue to move it forward that's what coaching is, is finding ways to put our guys in position to go have great success and go win. So that won't change and that that's that's going to be the case here as we get ready for Friday. >> I know we'll talk about this some tomorrow, but you know, this this game you've been on both sides of this thing, you know. Personally, what does it mean to you to get your hands on that trophy? >> It means everything. Uh to me right now for our football team, our program, I can't imagine anything meaning anything more. I I really can't, you know. So it's time for the trophy to come home. We got an unbelievable challenge in front of us against a really really good football team. Um but our guys they will. They'll be really excited to play. We got to go play really clean and really good football to to give us a chance to go win the game. But man, it means means everything. >> All right, thanks coach. >> Appreciate it.
